subject: economics
topicDisplay: Hl Extension Topics And Quantitative Analysis
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Forward guidance by a central bank means:
options: Buying foreign currency to influence the exchange rate
Communicating likely future interest rate policy to influence expectations
questions.explain: Forward guidance is the central bank signalling the probable future path of policy to shape expectations and influence current spending and borrowing.

questions.q: If a government wishes to reduce a current account deficit using expenditure-reducing policy, it might:
options: Cut taxes to boost spending on imports
Lower interest rates to encourage borrowing
Use contractionary fiscal/monetary policy to reduce demand for imports
questions.explain: Reducing aggregate demand lowers demand for imports, helping to narrow a current account deficit, albeit at the cost of slower growth.

questions.q: According to the classical (monetarist) view, the long-run aggregate supply curve is:
options: Vertical at the full-employment level of output
Horizontal at all levels of output
questions.explain: In the classical view LRAS is vertical at the full-employment (potential) level of output, so demand changes only affect the price level in the long run.

questions.q: Which combination represents the components of aggregate demand most likely to fall during a recession driven by low confidence?
questions.explain: Falling confidence reduces consumer spending and firms' investment, the two most cyclically sensitive components of AD.

questions.q: The government's inflation target in the UK is set as:
options: CPI of 2% (with a 1 percentage point tolerance band)
questions.explain: The UK target is a 2% CPI inflation rate, and the MPC must explain to the Chancellor if inflation moves more than 1 percentage point either side.

questions.q: Supernormal (abnormal) profit is earned when:
options: Average revenue exceeds average total cost
questions.explain: Supernormal profit exists when AR is greater than ATC, so the firm earns more than the normal return.

questions.q: In a one-shot Prisoner's Dilemma between two firms, the dominant strategy is typically to:
options: Defect (compete), leading to a worse outcome for both
questions.explain: Each firm's dominant strategy is to defect, producing a Nash equilibrium that is jointly worse than cooperating.

questions.q: A market-based supply-side policy is:
options: Reducing income tax rates to improve incentives to work
Government investment in state-run training schemes
Building infrastructure funded by the state
questions.explain: Market-based supply-side policies aim to improve incentives and competition through the market, such as cutting income tax to raise work incentives.

questions.q: For a perfectly competitive firm, the demand curve it faces is:
options: Perfectly elastic (horizontal) at the market price
questions.explain: A price-taking firm faces a horizontal, perfectly elastic demand curve at the prevailing market price.

questions.q: A cut in interest rates is most likely to cause the exchange rate to:
options: Depreciate as the return on domestic financial assets falls and capital flows out
Appreciate as hot money flows in
questions.explain: Lower interest rates reduce the relative return on domestic assets, encouraging capital outflows and tending to depreciate the currency.

questions.q: In the long run, firms in perfect competition earn:
questions.explain: Freedom of entry competes away supernormal profit, so firms make only normal profit in long-run equilibrium.

questions.q: If a firm pursues revenue maximisation rather than profit maximisation, it produces where:
questions.explain: Total revenue is maximised where marginal revenue equals zero.

questions.q: A market is described as a contestable market when:
options: There is a single dominant firm only
There are very high barriers to entry and exit
Barriers to entry and exit are low and there is a threat of new entrants
questions.explain: Contestable markets have low entry and exit barriers, so the threat of hit-and-run entry disciplines incumbents.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes a regressive tax?
options: A tax that takes a larger proportion of income from lower earners
A tax that takes a larger proportion of income from higher earners
A tax only paid by firms
A tax with the same average and marginal rate
questions.explain: A regressive tax, such as some indirect taxes, takes a higher proportion of income from those on lower incomes.

questions.q: The distinction between a budget (fiscal) deficit and the national debt is that:
options: The deficit is an annual flow; the national debt is the accumulated stock of borrowing
They are two names for the same thing
The deficit only includes interest payments
The national debt is annual; the deficit is the total stock
questions.explain: A fiscal deficit is the annual excess of spending over revenue (a flow); the national debt is the total stock of accumulated government borrowing.

questions.q: An increase in the rate of saving by households, other things equal, will:
options: Have no effect on national income
Increase injections into the circular flow
Increase a withdrawal from the circular flow
questions.explain: Saving is a withdrawal (leakage) from the circular flow, so higher saving reduces the flow of income unless matched by higher injections.

questions.q: Normal profit occurs when a firm earns:
options: Just enough return to keep resources in their current use (TR = TC including opportunity cost)
Total revenue greater than total cost
questions.explain: Normal profit is the minimum return needed to keep the entrepreneur in the industry, where TR equals TC including opportunity cost.

questions.q: The accelerator theory states that investment depends on:
options: The absolute level of national income
The rate of change of national income/output
questions.explain: The accelerator relates investment to the rate of change of output, so rising demand induces proportionally larger investment.

questions.q: The kinked demand curve model of oligopoly predicts that:
options: Firms always engage in price wars
questions.explain: The kink implies rivals match price cuts but not rises, so firms avoid changing price, giving price rigidity.

questions.q: If the marginal propensity to consume is 0.8 and there are no other withdrawals, the value of the multiplier is:
questions.explain: The multiplier equals 1/(1 − MPC) = 1/(1 − 0.8) = 1/0.2 = 5.

questions.q: The expectations-augmented (long-run) Phillips curve suggests that in the long run:
options: Higher inflation always lowers unemployment permanently
Unemployment returns to its natural rate regardless of the inflation rate
There is a permanent trade-off between inflation and unemployment
The Phillips curve is downward sloping forever
questions.explain: In the long run the economy returns to the natural rate of unemployment, so the long-run Phillips curve is vertical with no permanent trade-off.

questions.q: The Laffer curve suggests that beyond a certain tax rate:
options: Tax revenue continues to rise as rates rise
Lower tax rates always reduce revenue
Higher tax rates reduce total tax revenue because of disincentive effects
Tax revenue is unaffected by the tax rate
questions.explain: The Laffer curve implies that above an optimal rate, raising taxes reduces revenue as it discourages work, investment and encourages avoidance.

questions.q: The main aim of a central bank raising interest rates when the economy is overheating is to:
options: Reduce aggregate demand and inflationary pressure
questions.explain: Higher rates dampen borrowing and spending, reducing AD and easing demand-pull inflation when the economy is above capacity.

questions.q: Internal economies of scale that arise from spreading research and design costs over a larger output are called:
questions.explain: Technical economies include spreading large indivisible costs such as R&D and capital over greater output.

questions.q: For a perfectly competitive firm, marginal revenue equals:
questions.explain: Because the firm sells at a constant price, MR equals AR and equals price for every unit sold.

questions.q: A firm experiences increasing returns to scale when:
options: Output stays constant as inputs rise
Output rises proportionately more than all inputs
Output rises proportionately less than inputs
questions.explain: Increasing returns to scale occur when a given proportional increase in all inputs yields a larger proportional rise in output.

questions.q: In a contestable market, the threat of entry forces incumbent firms to:
options: Keep prices low and earn only normal profit in the long run
questions.explain: Because new firms could enter, incumbents keep prices and profits low to deter hit-and-run competition.

questions.q: Third-degree price discrimination requires the firm to:
options: Charge every consumer the same price
Separate markets with different price elasticities and prevent resale
Set price equal to marginal cost
questions.explain: Price discrimination needs market power, separable sub-markets with differing PED, and no arbitrage between them.

questions.q: The monetary transmission mechanism describes how:
options: Tax changes feed through to government revenue
A change in interest rates affects AD through channels such as borrowing, saving, asset prices and the exchange rate
questions.explain: The transmission mechanism is the process by which a change in the policy rate influences spending and inflation via borrowing costs, asset prices, confidence and the exchange rate.

questions.q: Frictional unemployment refers to people who are:
options: Unemployed because of a fall in aggregate demand
Temporarily between jobs while searching for new work
Out of work because of the time of year
Unemployed because their skills are obsolete
questions.explain: Frictional unemployment is short-term unemployment as workers move between jobs and search for suitable vacancies.
